title: More Arrests for Alleged Kirk Memorial Vandalism - NewsBreak
text:
By Roger Anderson ,
53 minutes ago Kerri Melissa Rollo and Kaylee Heather Rollo have reportedly launched a GoFundMe after being arrested for vandalizing a memorial for Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. Their alleged actions included kicking over candles and tearing down signs, resulting in significant online backlash and one sister losing her job. They have since claimed to be victims of doxxing and have raised $20,000 for legal funds.
Kaylee wrote, “After the recent events [of] Charlie Kirk’s death, my sibling and I are being doxxed online and my sibling was fired from their job.”
Kaylee added, “This is [a] direct violation of their first amendment rights and unconstitutional. This is unfortunate, but anything helps. Please help my sibling while they look for another job and stand against the tyranny that is creeping into the country.”
Both sisters face first-degree criminal mischief charges for alleged vandalism. Officials have stressed the importance of respect for memorials.
The Benton County Sheriff’s Office stated, “Sheriff Holloway takes acts of vandalism, particularly those directed toward community memorials, very seriously.”
Benton County Justice of the Peace Joseph Bollinger said, “Everyone has a right to be able to express their freedom of expression. But what the issue is, is when you trample on someone’s memorial—the human act of grieving.”
Bollinger stated, “You’re not just trampling on their freedom of expression; you’re trampling on the memory of a person.” He added, “You’re trampling on our Benton County values.”
Roger Anderson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
